description: We will we will rock you (with the help of some radar data)!
summary: We developed a project that shows how radar revealed ground movement in the 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye. We took two Sentinel-1 radar scenes, 29 January and 10 February 2023, from NASA’s ASF DAAC and produced an interferogram. The page explains how to read the colored fringes, where each full color cycle is about 2.8 cm of ground movement along the satellite’s line of sight. It also lets visitors compare before and after radar brightness with a slider. It addresses the challenge by turning complicated SAR observations into something the public can understand.
details:
What It Does:

The page shows the reader a real SAR result. It shows the interferogram in two views: full-color phase and phase drawn over the radar image. Next comes a before/after radar-brightness slider, a plain-language guide to reading the colors, and our interpretation. The interpretation notes that the image shows more than one cluster of strong deformation.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

We wanted to make radar results readable for people with no remote-sensing background. It can be used for education and for explaining how satellite data supports disaster response.

How We Made It:

We searched Sentinel-1 scenes in ASF Data Search Vertex and chose a pre-event scene (29 January 2023) and a post-event scene (10 February 2023). We ordered an InSAR product with a water mask, displacement and wrapped-phase outputs, and RTC products for the brightness comparison. The page is a single HTML file with CSS and a small amount of JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages. None of our team had programming experience, so we used Claude to write the page code and help us understand the data and tools.

Factors We Considered:

Our team chose a simple blog format over a dashboard. We used Sentinel-1 from the challenge’s resources. We kept the claims modest and listed the limits of the method on the page.
